Re-pointed 2026-08-03 from the retired shared host mvmcitest01 / ad.hraedon.com, which the SSH transport retirement took out of service; the host_id is historical and does not imply the lane executes on the DC. Lanes needing GPMC run on member-ws2025-disposable and reach this host for AD and SYSVOL, which is what wp2-native-import exercised end to end. Certifications produced against mvmcitest01 keep the environment recorded in their own manifests and are not retracted.

The estate client guest LabCL01. Qualified 2026-08-03 by a real 26200 client run that applied policy and observed CSE evidence (passed, no lane or control problems). Re-frozen 2026-07-29 from 24H2/26100 to 25H2/26200. Two measured limits shape every lane that uses it: the GroupPolicy module is absent (RSAT is a Feature-on-Demand the isolated estate cannot fetch), and the estate has never had an interactive logon, so user-scope resolution is WP-9 rather than WP-6.

The estate member server LabMS01, domain-joined, checkpoint-backed. Qualified 2026-08-03 by a 20/20 WP-3 run with zero environment violations. This is where WP-0, WP-1B, WP-2 and WP-3 actually execute: the same estate qualification also produced live-synthetic-registry-basic-20260803213433-5325 (WP-0), wp1b-writer-20260803213602-6066 (WP-1B) and wp2-native-import-20260803230132-8090 (WP-2) on this host. Qualifying the host does not itself expand any lane: that run exercised the same validate/import/export tranche as the shared host did, so secedit /configure and the wider template areas remain unexecuted work, not new evidence.

Recorded, not qualified (changed 2026-07-29): no current lane executes LGPO, so its hash is provenance only. Ruled 2026-08-03 that placing LGPO.exe on the estate is acceptable — disposable, checkpoint-backed guests, and the isolation invariant governs egress rather than what is deliberately placed inside — so WP-5 keeps its LGPO leg and this row is not pending because the tool was ruled out. It is pending because qualification is earned by execution: WP-5 must push the binary post-restore, verify it on the guest against a pinned SHA-256, and only then restore the check in frozen_environment_violations(). Do not flip this row on the strength of the ruling alone.

tools.notes: Qualified by the client-win11 qualification 2026-08-03. Two measured facts the rsop-endpoint lane is built on, both of which contradict the oracle this registry previously claimed: Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy is NOT available (no GroupPolicy module on the client), so the lane is gpresult.exe-only; and `gpresult /x` without /scope:computer exits 0, writes no file, and reports that the invoking account has no RSoP data. Assert on the artifact, never on the exit code.

Not used by any lane, and the reason is worth keeping. This row stood in for the user-scope gap: WP-6 forbids an interactive `whoami /groups` as the computer token, and the collection it described rode an interactive logon the estate did not have. The estate has one now (windows-evidence-lab, the `user-logged-on` checkpoint), and WP-9 was built without whoami: the principal's SID comes from an NTAccount translation, the winning values from the loaded hive at HKEY_USERS\<SID>, and the resultant set from gpresult /scope:user /user <principal>. Kept as a row rather than deleted so the gate it represented is visibly closed rather than quietly removed.

lanes.notes: Computer scope only, per the 2026-08-03 ruling; user scope and loopback are the rsop-user-loopback lane. BUILT AND CERTIFIED 2026-08-04 for lsdou-precedence: three consecutive passes (rsop-observe-20260804010341-7165, rsop-observe-20260804010551-9363, rsop-observe-20260804010738-5543), identical results, each from a clean endpoint. Extended 2026-08-04 to disabled-block-enforced (WI-029), which added block inheritance, enforced links, disabled links and per-side GPO status — and immediately found WI-031, a real defect in rsop.py's enforced-link precedence, now fixed and re-verified. Still partial: security filtering and WMI filters are absent from both topologies, and user scope is WP-9. It needs TWO oracles, not one: the Rsop document names the applied GPOs but carries zero RegistrySetting entries for the values set, so only the registry read answers which value won. See wp6b-results.md. Two corrections from measuring the client: Get-GPResultantSetOfPolicy is gone from the oracle because the module is absent, and whoami is gone from required_tools because the computer token comes from LDAP tokenGroups. Deterministic disposable topology per WP-6; no use of pre-existing lab GPOs; at least one control row must be decided by a mechanism Studio does not model. WMI filtering added 2026-08-04: certified first as a declared divergence (the model could not evaluate a filter and applied the GPO regardless), then WI-035 was fixed and it re-certified as an ordinary pass. The true-filtered control row is what makes the false row's absence meaningful, because a malformed WMI filter fails closed and looks identical.

lanes.oracle: gpresult.exe /x <file> /f /scope:user /user <DOMAIN>\<principal> on the client, parsed from the http://www.microsoft.com/GroupPolicy/Rsop namespace's UserResults section, plus the winning HKCU values read from the principal's loaded hive at HKEY_USERS\<SID>, plus GroupPolicy operational events -- 8005 for the completion of the principal's own processing pass, and 5311 for the loopback mode Windows actually used.
lanes.notes: BUILT AND CERTIFIED 2026-08-04 for three scenarios: user-side-disabled, loopback-merge and loopback-replace. This is the first external check rsop.py's user side and loopback have ever had. Measured facts the lane is built on, all taken before it was designed: an admin can capture another principal's user-scope RSoP from outside the session with /user (without it, gpresult exits 0 and writes nothing); the principal's hive is readable at HKEY_USERS\<SID>, and reading HKCU instead would return the HARNESS account's hive and report every value absent; and a scheduled task with -LogonType Interactive refreshes user policy inside the principal's session without needing its password. Event 5311 is the load-bearing control: under replace the expected observation is that a GPO's values are ABSENT, which is also what a run where loopback never engaged looks like, so a mode mismatch is inconclusive rather than a finding -- and it fired twice on real runs. CERTIFIED 2026-08-04 for user-side SECURITY FILTERING: Read+Apply, Read without Apply, and Apply through a group the principal belongs to, plus a separate scenario for an explicit deny ACE. That one was certified as a declared divergence first (the model could not express a deny), then WI-033 was fixed and it re-certified as an ordinary pass. The nesting row is gated on token collection -- the principal's own session token and the directory's tokenGroups -- because a token is minted at logon and never updated, so the lane restarts the client after authoring and verifies the NEW token holds the group. Still partial: slow-link and WMI outcomes on the user side are not covered, and the applied-GPO comparison is advisory rather than gated (WI-032). Requires the estate's user-logged-on checkpoint; the lane refuses to run without a verified console session.
